memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If, however, they do not redeem the field, or if they have sold it to
someone else, it can never be redeemed. When the field is released in the
Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD; it will
become priestly property'" - Lev 27:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Some things, once given to God, remained His permanently. A field that was
dedicated and not redeemed would, at the Jubilee, pass permanently into
the service of the sanctuary. It became holy — set apart for God for good.

There is a settledness in this. Not everything we give to God is meant to
be reclaimed. Some surrenders are meant to be final. Some things we place
in His hands should simply stay there, becoming permanently His.

Dear reader, think about the areas of your life that you keep offering to
God and then taking back — the same struggle surrendered a hundred times,
the same worry handed over and snatched again. What if some of these were
meant to become holy, given over for good?

There is freedom in a settled surrender. When something genuinely belongs
to God and we stop trying to reclaim it, the exhausting tug-of-war ends.

Jesus said whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever
loses their life for Me will find it (Matt 16:25). The things we grasp
most tightly are often the very things we most need to release
permanently into His keeping.

Hannah gave her son Samuel to the Lord and did not take him back; she
said, I have lent him to the LORD for his whole life (1 Sam 1:28). That
kind of final, unclutching surrender is not loss. It is where deep peace
is found.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have I been surrendering and reclaiming again and again?
2. Is there something meant to become permanently God's?
3. Where might a settled, final surrender bring me peace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, teach me the peace of surrender that does not reach back. Show me
what I am meant to give You for good, and help me leave it holy in Your
hands. Amen.
